tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Financial Literacy – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: Rahul earns Rs 40,000 a month. He spends Rs 24,000 on needs, Rs 10,000 on wants and saves the rest. Under the 50-30-20 rule, his savings rate is:
options: Above the recommended 20% of his income
Equal to the recommended 30% of his income
Below the recommended 20% of his income
Equal to the recommended 20% of his income

questions.question_text: Under the 50-30-20 rule, a person with a take-home income of Rs 60,000 should keep for needs and savings respectively:
Financial literacy is best described as the ability to:
options: Avoid the use of banks and other financial institutions
Predict the movements of the share prices in the market
Earn a higher income than the other persons in the same profession
Understand and use financial skills such as budgeting, saving and investing wisely

questions.question_text: The emergency fund of a salaried household is normally recommended to be about:
options: Half of the annual income kept in real estate
Twelve years of income kept in a fixed deposit
One month of living expenses kept in shares
Three to six months of living expenses kept in a liquid form

questions.question_text: Which of these is the best place to keep an emergency fund?
options: A small-cap equity fund that may fall sharply
A savings account or liquid fund that can be withdrawn at once
A five-year fixed deposit with a penalty on early withdrawal
A plot of land in a remote town

questions.question_text: A person invests Rs 10,000 at 8% simple interest per annum. The interest earned in 3 years is:
options: Rs 800

questions.question_text: Rs 10,000 is invested at 8% compounded annually. The amount after 2 years is:
The difference between compound and simple interest on Rs 10,000 at 10% p.a. for 2 years is:
options: Rs 100
Rs 200

questions.question_text: The Rule of 72 says that the time taken for money to double at 8% p.a. compound interest is about:
options: 9 years
12 years
8 years
6 years

questions.question_text: At an interest rate of 12% compounded annually, money doubles in roughly:
options: 3 years
6 years
12 years
9 years

questions.question_text: Inflation of 6% means that:
options: The purchasing power of a rupee falls by about 6% in a year
The income of the people rises by 6% in a year
The price of every good rises by exactly 6% in a year
The interest on savings rises by 6% every year

questions.question_text: If a deposit gives 7% interest and inflation is 5%, the approximate real rate of return is:
If a deposit gives 5% interest while inflation is 6%, the real return is:
options: About -1%, so the purchasing power falls
About 11%, so the purchasing power rises
About 0%, so the purchasing power is the same
About 1%, so the purchasing power rises

questions.question_text: Rs 1,00,000 today at 6% inflation will have the purchasing power of about what amount after 12 years (Rule of 72 for doubling prices)?
A good budget is one in which:
options: Planned expenses do not exceed expected income and some savings are made
Only the large expenses are recorded and small expenses are ignored
Expenses are always equal to income, leaving nothing for savings
Income is assumed to be higher than what the person is likely to earn

questions.question_text: A household with income of Rs 50,000, fixed expenses Rs 30,000 and variable expenses Rs 15,000 has a surplus of:
Which of the following is a fixed expense in a household budget?
options: Entertainment and movies
House rent and EMI of a loan
Eating out at restaurants
Clothing for festivals

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a discretionary expense?
options: Electricity bill
Holiday trip
School fees
Loan EMI

questions.question_text: "Pay yourself first" means:
options: Setting aside the savings as soon as the income is received
Spending on your wants before paying the bills
Investing only when the income increases
Paying the loans after the savings are over

questions.question_text: Net worth of a person is:
options: Total income minus total expenses
Total assets minus total liabilities
Total savings plus total income
Total assets plus total liabilities

questions.question_text: A person has assets of Rs 25 lakh (house, savings) and liabilities of Rs 8 lakh (home loan). Net worth is:
options: Rs 25 lakh
Rs 33 lakh
Rs 8 lakh
Rs 17 lakh

questions.question_text: Which of these is an asset?
options: Education loan
Credit card outstanding
Fixed deposit in a bank
Pending electricity bill

questions.question_text: The credit score in India (CIBIL) ranges from:
A CIBIL score of 780 is generally considered:
options: Average and has no effect on the loans
Good and helps in getting loans at better rates
Poor and leads to rejection of loans
Invalid since the maximum is 750

questions.question_text: Which of these habits improves a credit score?
options: Paying EMIs and credit card dues on time
Applying for many loans at once
Making only the minimum payment on the credit card for months
Closing the oldest credit account

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Financial Literacy – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: A credit card has an interest rate of 3.5% per month on unpaid dues. This is about what percentage per year (simple multiplication)?
Using a credit card, a person pays only the "minimum amount due" every month. The likely result is:
options: The balance is cleared in a month
The balance carries interest and the debt grows
No interest is charged on the balance
The credit limit is increased free of cost

questions.question_text: The interest-free period of a credit card applies if:
options: The card is used for cash withdrawal
Only half the bill is paid
The full bill is paid by the due date
Only the minimum amount is paid

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a SMART financial goal?
options: Save some money for the future whenever it is possible
Spend less on shopping from the next month onwards
Save Rs 1.2 lakh in 12 months for a laptop by saving Rs 10,000 a month
Become rich in the course of time without any fixed plan

questions.question_text: The principle "don't put all your eggs in one basket" refers to:
options: Inflation protection
Compounding of returns
Liquidity
Diversification of investments

questions.question_text: Which pair shows the usual relation between risk and return?
options: Higher risk investments have a lower expected return
All investments have the same return
Risk and return are never related
Higher risk investments have a higher expected return

questions.question_text: Which of the following is generally the safest investment for a risk-averse person?
options: Penny stocks that are recommended in a social media group
Shares of a newly started company listed on a stock exchange
Cryptocurrency that is traded on an online platform
Government securities and bank deposits within the insured limit

questions.question_text: Time value of money means that:
options: A rupee today is worth more than a rupee in the future
Money loses value only with the inflation
A rupee in the future is worth more than a rupee today
The value of money does not change with time

questions.question_text: The present value of Rs 11,000 receivable after one year at 10% is:
A person saves Rs 5,000 per month for 12 months in a recurring deposit at 0% interest. The total savings are:
A person saves Rs 2,000 a month for 3 years. Without any interest, the total saved is:
Which statement about a debt trap is correct?
options: Taking a loan always improves the financial position of the borrower
Borrowing to repay old loans at high interest can push a person deeper into debt
A debt trap is impossible with the use of credit cards by borrowers
A debt trap arises only from saving too much out of the income

questions.question_text: The debt-to-income ratio helps a lender to judge:
options: The age at which the borrower expects to retire from work
The profession which the borrower has been following
The place where the borrower has been residing for years
Whether the borrower can afford to repay a new loan

questions.question_text: As a thumb rule, total EMIs should not exceed what share of the monthly income?
options: About 40%
About 65%
About 80%
About 90%

questions.question_text: If a person's monthly income is Rs 80,000, the maximum EMI by the 40% rule is:
The Reserve Bank of India's financial literacy initiative for the rural people is run through:
options: Stock exchanges
Insurance companies
Post offices only
Financial Literacy Centres

questions.question_text: The National Strategy for Financial Education in India is developed by:
options: The Supreme Court
NCFE under the RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA
The Election Commission
The Ministry of Defence alone

questions.question_text: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is aimed at:
options: Giving cheap loans to large industries for new factories
Providing free education to the children of poor families
Providing free housing to the families below the poverty line
Financial inclusion through basic bank accounts for all households

questions.question_text: A basic savings bank deposit account (BSBDA) is characterised by:
options: No facility for deposits
Zero minimum balance and limited free transactions
No facility for withdrawals
High minimum balance and many charges

questions.question_text: A benefit given with Jan Dhan accounts is:
options: A RuPay debit card with an accident insurance cover
A free luxury car for the account holders every year
Free foreign travel for the account holders and family
A guaranteed profit on shares for the account holders

questions.question_text: Direct benefit transfer sends subsidies:
options: Straight into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries
Through the middlemen who work in the villages
To the post office, to be handed out in cash
To the local shops, to be given as goods

questions.question_text: KYC stands for:
options: Know Your Credit
Keep Your Cash
Key Yearly Charges
Know Your Customer

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a document commonly accepted as the proof of identity for KYC?
options: Credit card bill
Electricity bill
School report card
Aadhaar or passport

questions.question_text: A caller asks for the OTP of your account for a "KYC update". The correct response is to:
options: Share only the first three digits of the OTP received
Refuse, as no bank asks for an OTP over a phone call
Share it if the caller knows your name and your address
Share the OTP so that the account gets updated at once

questions.question_text: A message says you have won a lottery and asks for a processing fee. This is most likely:
options: An insurance bonus
A legitimate prize from the bank
A fraud or phishing attempt
A government scheme

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Financial Literacy – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: If you lose money by an unauthorised online transaction, you should first:
options: Wait for a week to see if the money returns
Share your PIN with the caller who offers help
Inform the bank immediately and block the card or account
Post about it on social media only

questions.question_text: Under RBI rules, if the customer reports an unauthorised transaction within 3 working days where the fault is of the bank, the customer's liability is:
options: Half amount
Full amount
Zero

questions.question_text: A strong password is one that:
options: Is the word "password" followed by the number one
Mixes letters, numbers and symbols and is not shared
Is the name of the pet of the holder of the account
Is the date of birth of the holder of the account

questions.question_text: The RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme deals with:
options: Complaints against the municipal bodies of the local area
Complaints against the schools and the colleges of the city
Customer complaints against banks and other regulated entities
Complaints against the police and the other law enforcers

questions.question_text: Before approaching the ombudsman, a customer should first:
options: Write to the Prime Minister about the complaint
Go to court and file a civil suit against the bank
Complain to the bank and give it time to reply
Stop using the bank account and close it at once

questions.question_text: The main aim of consumer protection in financial services is to:
options: Protect customers from unfair practices and mis-selling
Reduce the number of bank branches in the country
Stop the customers from taking loans from the banks
Increase the profits of banks and other lenders

questions.question_text: "Mis-selling" of a financial product means:
options: Selling it at its cost price to the buyers without any profit
Selling it online instead of in a physical branch
Selling it by giving wrong or incomplete information to the buyer
Selling it at a discount to the existing customers

questions.question_text: Before buying an insurance policy, a person should:
options: Ignore the fine print
Buy it on the basis of the friend's word only
Read the terms, exclusions and the premium carefully
Buy the one with the highest commission to the agent

questions.question_text: A salesman says a ULIP gives "guaranteed 20% returns". This claim is likely to be:
options: Backed by the RBI, which guarantees all the returns
Backed by the government, which guarantees all the returns
Correct, as ULIPs are fixed-income products by their nature
Misleading, since market-linked returns cannot be guaranteed

questions.question_text: A Ponzi scheme is one in which:
options: The scheme is run and guaranteed by the RBI
Early investors are paid out of the money of new investors
The money is invested only in the government bonds
Returns are paid out of the real profits of a business

questions.question_text: A warning sign of a fraudulent investment scheme is:
options: Very high guaranteed returns with little or no risk
Audited accounts published every year for investors
Registration of the scheme with SEBI before launch
Clear disclosure of risks in the offer document

questions.question_text: The practice of making a person who lacks knowledge to take a loan beyond his repayment capacity is called:
options: Micro-financing
Predatory lending
Syndication
Securitisation

questions.question_text: The EMI on a loan depends on:
options: The principal, the rate of interest and the tenure
The tenure of the loan alone, irrespective of the rate
The principal of the loan alone, irrespective of the rate
The rate of interest alone, irrespective of the tenure

questions.question_text: If the tenure of a loan is increased, the EMI will:
options: Remain the same, and the total interest will remain the same
Rise, and the total interest paid will fall
Fall, and the total interest paid will fall
Fall, but the total interest paid will rise

questions.question_text: A reducing balance rate of 10% versus a flat rate of 10% on the same loan: the effective cost is:
options: The same for both
Zero for the flat rate
Higher for the reducing balance loan
Higher for the flat rate loan

questions.question_text: A loan of Rs 1,00,000 at a flat rate of 10% p.a. for 2 years. The total interest is:
In the above case the total repayment is Rs 1,20,000. The monthly instalment (24 months) is:
A loan taken to buy an appreciating asset such as a house is often called:
options: Bad debt in all cases
A gift
Good debt, if it is affordable
Free money

questions.question_text: Borrowing on a credit card to fund a holiday trip is generally regarded as:
options: Bad debt, as it has a high interest and creates no asset
Good debt, as the trip will appreciate in value over time
Tax-saving debt, as the interest is deducted from the income
Free credit, as no interest is charged on the card

questions.question_text: A person who gets Rs 20,000 per month from the rent of a flat is earning:
options: Capital gain
Active income
Salary
Passive income

questions.question_text: Which of these is an active income?
options: Interest on deposits
Salary from employment
Rent from property
Dividend from shares

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a capital gain?
options: Pension received every month after retirement
Profit on the sale of shares bought earlier at a lower price
Interest received on a savings bank account
Salary received every month from an employer

questions.question_text: Financial planning begins with:
options: Taking a loan from a bank for a large purchase
Setting financial goals and finding the present financial position
Investing in shares of a company that is popular
Buying an insurance policy from the nearest agent

questions.question_text: The correct order of the steps in financial planning is:
options: Implement, review, set goals, assess position, make a plan
Set goals, assess position, make a plan, implement and review
Assess position, review, implement, make a plan, set goals
Make a plan, set goals, implement, assess position, review

questions.question_text: Life-cycle financial planning suggests that a young earner should:
options: Start saving early to benefit from compounding
Wait until retirement to start saving
Borrow as much as possible
Avoid insurance

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Financial Literacy – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: Person A invests Rs 5,000 a month from age 25 to 35 and stops; person B invests Rs 5,000 a month from 35 to 60. Both earn the same rate. A's early money does well because:
options: It is free from tax
It earns a higher rate of return
It compounds for a longer time
It is invested for more number of months

questions.question_text: A sign of good financial habits is:
options: Borrowing money for meeting the daily needs
Tracking expenses and avoiding impulse purchases
Spending more than the income earned every month
Ignoring bills until a final notice is received

questions.question_text: Digital financial literacy includes:
options: Learning to design websites for a business
Learning to repair computers and mobile phones
Safe use of UPI, net banking and mobile wallets
Learning to write software code for apps

questions.question_text: A "no cost EMI" offer on a purchase usually means that:
options: The loan is made free of any charge by the law
The bank has agreed to bear all the costs itself
The interest is built into the price or covered by a fee
There is no legal obligation on the buyer to pay

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a regulator of the financial system in India?
options: NITI Aayog
IRDAI
SEBI
RBI

questions.question_text: PFRDA regulates:
options: The stock market, including the mutual funds
The insurance sector, including the health policies
The banking sector, including the cooperative banks
The pension sector, including the National Pension System

questions.question_text: IRDAI regulates:
options: The insurance sector
The stock market
The pension sector
The commodity market

questions.question_text: SEBI regulates:
options: The post office savings and the small savings schemes
The securities market and mutual funds
The insurance companies and the brokers of insurance
The banks and the non-banking finance companies

questions.question_text: Deposits in banks in India are insured up to what amount per depositor per bank by DICGC?
options: Rs 1 lakh
Rs 10 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 25 lakh

questions.question_text: A person has Rs 8 lakh in a savings account and Rs 3 lakh in a fixed deposit in the same bank, and the bank fails. The amount insured by DICGC is:
options: Rs 3 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 8 lakh
Rs 11 lakh

questions.question_text: Suppose the same person holds Rs 5 lakh each in two different banks, both failing. The insured amount in total is:
options: Rs 5 lakh
Rs 15 lakh
Rs 20 lakh
Rs 10 lakh

questions.question_text: The financial inclusion index measures:
options: Access to and usage of the financial services by the people
The income earned by banks in the financial year
The number of the stock brokers working in the country
The number of the loans given by banks in a year

questions.question_text: The factor that most improves a person's chance of getting a loan is:
options: Many unpaid dues on the earlier loans and cards
The absence of any bank account in the person's name
A steady income and a good credit history
Frequent changes of job in short periods of time

questions.question_text: A person with a net monthly income of Rs 50,000 wants to save for a Rs 6 lakh goal in 3 years. The monthly saving needed (ignoring interest) is:
Which of the following increases a person's net worth?
options: A new loan taken and spent on a holiday trip
A car bought on credit with a high EMI
Profit earned on investments that were made earlier
Expenses that are not recorded in any book

questions.question_text: The "liquidity" of an investment means:
options: How much return it is expected to earn every year
How quickly it can be turned into cash without a loss
How long the investment will continue to exist
How safe the invested money is from the loss of value

questions.question_text: Which one of these is most liquid?
options: A plot of land
A house
Gold jewellery
Cash in a savings account

questions.question_text: The three objectives of an investor are:
options: Price, quantity and quality
Salary, loan and tax
Cash, credit and cheque
Safety, liquidity and return

questions.question_text: An investor in his sixties who needs regular income would prefer an investment which has:
options: No liquidity
Highly volatile prices
Safety and regular income
Very high risk and high returns

questions.question_text: Mrs Sharma puts Rs 1,00,000 in a fixed deposit at 7% compounded annually for 2 years. The maturity amount is:
Which of the following correctly shows the effect of inflation on a fixed pension?
options: The pension doubles every year
The real value of the pension falls over time
The pension is unaffected by the inflation
The real value of the pension rises over time

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT a part of a personal budget?
options: Expenses
Income
Stock exchange index
Savings

questions.question_text: Zero-based budgeting at the personal level means:
options: Keeping zero savings at the end of every month
Spending nothing at all for the entire month
Giving every rupee of income a purpose, so that income less spending and savings is zero
Having zero income for a period of the year

questions.question_text: A proper use of a credit card is:
options: Paying the full bill every month before the due date
Using up the maximum limit available every month
Withdrawing cash and paying the bill late each time
Paying only the minimum amount due each month

questions.question_text: The most important step towards financial security for a young earner is to:
options: Take more loans so that more assets can be bought
Delay saving until the income grows to a higher level
Spend less than earned and invest the difference regularly
Spend the whole income every month on the wants
